plos-pone-0003440: Neuroscientists read the chemistry of birdsong in this 2008 paper. plos-pone-0003540: Memory researchers found an enzyme that cements recalled memories in the 2008 paper. plos-pone-0003640: In 2008, a team tested a shortcut for counting new HIV cases in rural South Africa. plos-pone-0003740: In 2008, Iliopoulos, Malizos, and Oikonomou hunted arthritis genes two ways at once. plos-pone-0003840: In 2008, Gaseitsiwe, Valentini, and Mahdavifar turned a cancer trick on tuberculosis. plos-pone-0003940: In 2008, Luchman, Benediktsson, and Villemaire tied prostate cancer speed to gene timing. Losing the PTEN tumor suppressor early sped up precancerous prostate growth in mice. The timing result shows when a cancer gene falls matters as much as whether it falls.
plos-pone-0004040: In 2008, Manos Tsakiris asked what makes a face feel like mine. Volunteers watched their own face being touched while feeling the touch themselves. plos-pone-0004140: In 2009, Cudney-Bueno, Lavin, and Marinone found reserves working fast. Marine reserves boosted nearby fish through larval dispersal. plos-pone-0004240: In 2009, Fujimoto, Miyasaka, and Koyanagi found skinny mice missing a protein. KRAP-deficient mice resisted diet-induced obesity. plos-pone-0004340: In 2009, José, Govezensky, and García traced the code of life's birth. Two primeval RNA codes were proposed as ancestors of the standard genetic code. The extended RNA code type I fit best. The theory grounds code evolution in the RNA world.
plos-pone-0341940: Older adults with intellectual disability are often left out of community life. The MATILDA intervention was designed to change that, and this paper reports a feasibility trial testing whether it can work in practice. The results show whether boosting community participation this way is doable — and what a full trial would need.
plos-pone-0358940: Cancer symptoms don’t arrive alone — they cluster and feed each other. This scoping review gathered studies using symptom network analysis in gastric cancer patients, mapping how symptoms like pain, fatigue, and nausea connect. The networks reveal which symptoms sit at the hub, pointing nurses toward the most strategic targets for relief.
plos-pone-0358240: Machines monitored by different sensors speak different data languages — and models trained on one often fail on another. This paper built a cross-sensor domain adaptation network for multi-point mechanical fault diagnosis. The adaptation lets diagnostic models trained on one sensor type work reliably on another.
plos-pone-0356240: Training caregivers of children with cerebral palsy in rural Malawi faces steep practical barriers. This paper identified the facilitators and barriers to implementing a caregiver-led training programme there. The findings shape realistic implementation — built around what Malawian families can actually do.
plos-pone-0349740: Ramadan’s diurnal intermittent fasting measurably changes the living brain. This paired-pulse transcranial magnetic stimulation study tracked longitudinal changes in intracortical excitability across the fasting month. The results reveal how the cortex adapts its excitability to the fast — neuroscience meeting lived faith.
plos-pone-0357040: Small river basins flood fast — and need forecasts to match. This data-intelligence-driven approach combined a BiLSTM model with a ‘631’ response mechanism for flood forecasting and early warning. The integrated system turns data into life-saving lead time for vulnerable communities.
plos-pone-0342140: The pandemic’s mental health toll fell heavily on middle-aged and older adults. This scoping review mapped the changes in their mental health outcomes across the COVID-19 years. The synthesis reveals a burden that health systems are still struggling to address.
plos-pone-0355540: Biological regulation is hierarchical — and modeling it demands formal tools. This paper developed signal hierarchical Petri nets with formal semantics for the hierarchical regulatory control of biological systems. The mathematical framework gives systems biologists a rigorous language for layered regulation.
plos-pone-0355940: Can learning to cook actually improve what people eat? This systematic review asked whether developing cooking skills influences nutritional status and diet. The synthesized evidence tests a beloved public health assumption — with implications for every cooking class funded in the name of nutrition.
plos-pone-0356340: This entry is a correction notice, not a research finding. It amends the comparison of parameters derived from a three-minute all-out running test against classical exercise benchmarks. Readers should consult the corrected version for the accurate exercise physiology record.
plos-pone-0355740: Mapping brain tissue damage in 3D could transform neuropathology — if AI can segment the slabs. This paper presented a public, generalizable AI tool for automated segmentation of coronal brain tissue slabs for 3D neuropathology. The open tool brings quantitative 3D brain mapping within reach of any brain bank.
plos-pone-0356140: Self-driving cars in cities need wireless that survives concrete canyons. This paper proposed a dual-polarized RIS-assisted spatial modulation architecture for robust vehicular communications in urban environments. The reconfigurable-surface design keeps vehicles connected where signals ordinarily die.
plos-pone-0355840: Cave-dwelling bats in southeastern Nigeria harbor Trypanosoma livingstonei — near people’s homes. This paper presented evidence from peri-domestic roosts. The findings flag a zoonotic interface where bat parasites and human settlements meet — warranting surveillance before spillover, not after.
plos-pone-0354840: Alpine brambles — the Rubus genus — defy tidy species boundaries. This paper used untargeted metabolomics as a new lens for assessing their taxonomic boundaries. The chemical fingerprints reveal relationships that morphology obscures — reshaping the taxonomy of these mountain berries.
plos-pone-0352640: Hibernating black bears sleep differently than their wakeful cousins — and AI can score it. This paper achieved automated sleep scoring in hibernating and non-hibernating American black bears. The findings open a window on one of nature’s most extreme physiological feats.
europmc-pmc2860140: Muscles that shrug off insulin drive diabetes, and this 2010 review asks why. The authors trace the pathogenesis of insulin resistance in skeletal muscle. Their overview connects faulty signaling to the disease. The review remains a primer on muscle's role in diabetes.
europmc-pmc2872640: The genome's dark matter, mysterious RNA transcripts, mostly maps to known genes after all. This 2010 paper shows most dark matter transcripts associate with known genes. The authors' analysis shrank the mystery. Their result refocused the hunt for truly novel RNAs.
europmc-pmc2888740: Drink's link to stroke is not one-size-fits-all. This 2010 review and meta-analysis weighs alcohol against the risk of illness and death from different stroke types. The authors find the risk varies by stroke kind. Their careful split refined drinking advice.
europmc-pmc2909940: Math models of cells need a shared home. This 2010 paper presents the BioModels Database, a curated and annotated resource for published quantitative kinetic models. The authors' library lets researchers reuse and test models. Their resource became systems biology's model shelf.
europmc-pmc2920840: Iron is life's contested prize. This 2010 review narrates the battle for iron between bacterial pathogens and their vertebrate hosts. europmc-pmc2954140: Computer programs can ease anxiety and low mood. This 2010 pooled study finds online therapy works well and suits patients with anxiety and depression. europmc-pmc3021840: Brain signal analysis got open tools. This 2011 paper brings FieldTrip, free software for studying MEG, EEG, and brain implants. The authors' toolbox became a lab staple. europmc-pmc6602440: Comparing gene activity between tumors and healthy tissue is central to cancer research - GEPIA2 makes it point-and-click. europmc-pmc6616540: Heart disease does not strike everyone equally: age and sex reshape the risk. europmc-pmc6627940: Glycine - the simplest amino acid - moonlights far beyond building proteins: it feeds antioxidant defenses and one-carbon metabolism. europmc-pmc6675740: Deadly falciparum malaria has retreated in many places since 2000 - but not everywhere. europmc-pmc6702140: NAD+ - the cell's energy currency - dwindles with age, and a vitamin B3 cousin called nicotinamide riboside may top it up. europmc-pmc6753140: Tumors with heavy mutation loads should be sitting ducks for immunotherapy - yet some hide. This study shows DNA methylation loss helps mutation-laden tumors evade the immune system. The epigenetic cloak explains a paradox and points to drugs that could strip it away.
europmc-pmc6770940: Plants under drought or salt stress drown in reactive oxygen - and fight back with chemistry. This review details the ascorbate-glutathione pathway: the antioxidant assembly line that detoxifies ROS in stressed crops. Strengthening the pathway could breed tougher plants.
europmc-pmc6774040: Wearable electronics need conductors that bend and stretch.
